subject: Hosted API: accumulated batches causing p95/p99 regression — immediate action plan
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@clearhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T08:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API — sudden p95/p99 regression, affecting billing service

Hi Naomi,

We started seeing a sharp increase in response times against the hosted API this morning (around 07:30 PDT). p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s, p99 up to ~3.4s, and our 5xx rate climbed to ~4.8% (was ~0.2%). This is affecting our billing reconciliation jobs — several invoices failed due to timeouts.

Attached is a short perf snapshot and a sample trace (sample_trace.har). We can share more telemetry if it helps. Notably we see a lot of requests reporting "queued"/"batching_wait" in the client-side logs.

Can you please triage and advise ETA for a mitigation? If this requires a config change on your side, we need a timeline — this is blocking our nightly runs.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Engineering Ops — ClearHealth
Attachments: perf_snapshot_20270515.json, sample_trace.har

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API — sudden p95/p99 regression, affecting billing service

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We're escalating immediately. I'm looping in Jonas (runtime infra) and Marissa (customer success/ops) to triage.

Immediate asks:
- Jonas/infra: can you look for correlated signals (batch size distribution, queue depth, KV cache hit rate) across the time window starting 07:00 PDT?
- Marissa: I'm going to coordinate the customer comms and bridge. Please prep the runbook for emergency mitigations (smaller max_batch_size, temporary routing to lower-capacity model variants, and a short-term rate policy).

Sanjay — we'll send an ETA in 15 minutes and propose a 30-minute bridge if we need to execute config changes.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc:
Date: 2027-05-15T08:39:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API — sudden p95/p99 regression, affecting billing service

Quick initial read from infra: correlates exactly with a spike in queued batch depth across a subset of hosts in us-west-2 starting ~07:15 PDT. Observations:
- Average batch depth on affected hosts increased from ~6 to ~22 during the spike window.
- KV cache miss rate rose by ~30% (cold prefixes from a large import job reported by customer).
- There was a slow drain on the request queue which amplified per-request latency (allocation waiting for batch fill).
- No recent kernel-level deploys that look suspicious; however, INF-2145 (large S3 import job change) rolled earlier today for a different tenant which increased memory pressure on the same instance pools.

Immediate recommended mitigations (can be applied live):
1) Reduce max_batch_size to 8 on the affected pools to lower queue wait amplification.
2) Enforce per-customer queue caps for background/import-style workloads.
3) Warm KV caches for ClearHealth prefixes where feasible.
4) Short-term routing: fall back to a lower-capacity model variant for long-running background jobs.

I've opened INF-2145 and attached a prod snapshot (prod-snapshot.txt) with host-level metrics. If Naomi wants, I can execute (1) and (4) now; these are low-risk and reversible.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API — immediate runbook + suggested customer remediation

Thanks team. Adding a short emergency runbook we can run from the console:
- Step A: Decrease max_batch_size and max_batch_delay for the us-west-2 pools that host ClearHealth traffic.
- Step B: Apply a soft cap on concurrent background workers (customer side) — ask ClearHealth to pause the bulk import for ~90 minutes while we normalize queues.
- Step C: Toggle aggressive KV prefetch for their known prefixes for the next 2 hours.
- Step D: Monitor p95/p99 and 5xx rate in the bridge; rollback changes if error rate increases.

Customer-facing note: suggest offering their ops team a one-time credit for the window and a follow-up postmortem review. We should capture the telemetry and root cause steps in a postmortem doc (link in thread).

I've saved the runbook edits to runbook-emergency-adjustments.md and I'm standing by for permission to apply live adjustments.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API — accumulated batches causing p95/p99 regression — immediate action plan

Hi Sanjay — quick update from the triage: we see queued batch depth climbing at ~07:15 PDT which amplified p95/p99. Our infra team recommends a short set of mitigations we can apply immediately and we've prepared a runbook. Proposed immediate actions (apply in next 10 minutes):
1) Reduce max_batch_size to 8 on the affected us-west-2 pool (low risk, reversible).
2) Temporarily route long-running background jobs to a lower-capacity model variant.
3) Enable aggressive KV prefetch for your known prefixes for a 2-hour window.

We request ClearHealth pause the bulk import job for ~90 minutes while we run these mitigations and monitor. If you approve, we'll execute the changes and schedule a 30-minute bridge at 09:30 PDT to review metrics.

We will also provision a post-incident credit for the impacted window and follow up with a formal postmortem. ETA for first results: 10–15 minutes after we apply the config changes.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Contact: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
